title: His teacher's advice and the fact his mother never saw him play
summary: Greer repeats advice from his teacher and regrets that his parents never saw him perform.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You know what else she said. She died when she was 90-some years old. The last time I saw her, I played at the Hollywood Bowl in California and she was 90-some years old, and she come back, this old lady and she told all her friends, 'That's one of my pupils', hugged me and kissed me and cried.
You know a funny thing, not to be sentimental, my whole career as a professional, my mother never heard me play.

My father never heard me play. My sisters never heard me play. My brother heard me play once. And I played all over the world. There's one thing I regret, my mother could never seem me in action. She kept up with what I was doing and was very proud, but to actually see me play. No. Never saw me play.
We never played -- we played everywhere--

Oh, a lot of the boys have been down to my house to visit, but my mother never saw me play. Never. That's one thing that always stuck. You know, parents like to see their kids. Never. They heard about me because I was a notorious character. But they never saw me in action.

Another thing my teacher told me, she told me don't you ever forget it. She say, "Sonny, appearance is half the battle. When you look good, don't -- that's half of the battle. When you look good and can play good, you got it made" I never forgot it. Whenever I got on the stage, I never forgot how that guy looked -- I'm sharp as a wedding duck. You better believe it. I never had to do nothing but (unintelligible) I was young, pretty and rich, man. You better believe it.
